The UPI photo caption indexes a 75–29 confidence vote, but the original returned 403. The tally is held out until an inspectable original is obtained; coalition size 75 is independently verified by JTA.

United Torah Judaism left Barak’s coalition in September 1999 (Kenig; Kenig and Rahat); a UTJ MK told the Knesset on 8 September 1999 that the faction was in opposition. The day is not recorded, so the member list is dated by month only. The signed and dated letter of its five MKs to Ehud Barak, or its incoming stamp in the Prime Minister’s Office register (4–8 September 1999), would settle it; 5 September is only a lead.

Meretz after its ministers resigned (24 June 2000): whether and when the faction formally left the coalition is not recorded. Its MKs said in the Knesset on 26 June and 3 July 2000 that it was still in the coalition, and on 4 July one spoke of support from outside; two studies say it left in June. The Meretz faction’s or executive’s resolution ending its coalition membership, its notice to Barak, or a dated Knesset or coalition-chair statement separating the faction’s departure from the ministers’ resignations would settle it. Shown with an unknown role, not counted.

Roman Bronfman and Alexander Tsinker, July 1999: Bronfman said in 2001 that he had never been part of Barak’s coalition. The member lists count them within Yisrael BaAliyah’s 6 seats from 6 July 1999 until their faction split on 20 July, as the coalition of 75 (JTA) and Uzi Landau in the Knesset (28 July 1999: “originally 75”, then 73) do. The roll call of the confidence vote of 6 July 1999, or a dated statement by the two MKs from that week, would settle it.

Gesher after David Levy’s term as minister ended (30 July 2002): whether the faction stayed in Sharon’s coalition is not recorded. A Gesher MK called it a coalition faction in the Knesset on 27 May 2002; on 4 November 2002 another MK spoke of Gesher as having left. Gesher’s faction decision or David Levy’s dated withdrawal letter of 28–30 July 2002 covering both its MKs, or a coalition list from after his resignation, would settle it.

Gesher, August 2000: David Levy and Maxim Levy stayed in the One Israel faction until 7 March 2001. Kenig (Israel Democracy Institute) says Gesher’s MKs left the coalition with David Levy, whose term as Foreign Minister ended on 4 August 2000, but no dated Gesher declaration naming both brothers has been found, so Maxim Levy’s place in the coalition, and the day Gesher left it, are not recorded. Shown with an unknown role, not counted.
